newsitem.title: CHINA: China stock indices close mostly higher.
newsitem.headline: China stock indices close mostly higher.

text.p: China's stock indices ended mostly higher on Thursday with the Shanghai foreign currency B market the one dissenting voice in the crowd.
Shanghai's foreign currency B shares edged down on Thursday in stable trading, erasing morning gains, brokers said.
The B share market had gained in Thursday morning trading on buying of recently listed issues, including Shanghai Zhenhua Port Machinery Co Ltd and Hainan Airlines Co, they said.
However, the B index slipped 0.121 points or 0.16 percent to 74.182 points at the close on moderate turnover of $7.132 million, compared with $9.841 million on Wednesday.
"The B shares were relatively stable and turnover was very light," said an analyst at Shenyin & Wanguo Securities.
"Trading will be stable in the short term and I don't expect any bad news," he said.
Of 46 B shares, 42 traded with 15 down, 16 up and 11 unchanged.
Shanghai Yaohua Pilkington Glass Co was the biggest B share loser on speculative selling, plunging $0.030 or 9.09 percent to $0.300.

Zhenhua Port, which listed earlier this week, was the most actively traded share and the top gainer in the falling market. The stock surged $0.052 or 9.85 percent to $0.580 on volume of around 2.1 million shares.
Domestic currency A shares reversed early losses on buying of companies which also had H shares listed in Hong Kong, brokers said.
H shares, shares of Chinese firms listed in Hong Kong, had recently performed strongly, they said.
The Shanghai A share index jumped 29.390 points or 2.40 percent to 1,255.191 points on turnover of 3.074 billion yuan against 2.788 billion yuan on Wednesday.
Shanghai's SSE30 blue chip rose 61.517 points or 1.67 percent to 3,749.004 points.
Shenzhen's hard currency B share index ended minimally higher in dull trading, helped by institutional support just before the close, brokers said.
They said they expected the index to move around current levels in the short term due to an absence of new incentives.
The B index inched up 0.03 points or 0.02 percent to 129.99 on turnover of HK$45 million against HK$46 million on Wednesday.
"Despite the rise, sentiment in the market did not improve," an analyst at J&A Securities (HK) said. "The index is expected to hold steady in the near future."
Shenzhen's domestic A share index gained 3.87 points or 0.96 percent to 407.39 points on turnover of 4.4 billion yuan against 4.0 billion yuan in the previous session.

A spurt of buying of Beijing Orient Electronics just before the market closed helped lift the B share index, brokers said. The stock closed up HK$0.03 to HK$3.95 on heavy volume of 1.6 million shares.
The company on Monday posted a 29 percent year-on-year jump in its 1997 interim net profits, which reached 68.72 million yuan under international accounting standards.
Shenzhen Nanshan Power Station was the best B share performer, rising HK$0.24 or 5.21 percent to HK$4.85 on volume 439,901 shares.
Bengang Steel was the most actively traded B counter on volume of 1.77 million shares, putting on a meagre HK$0.01 to HK$2.10 against its recent offer price of HK$2.38.
